newsitem.title: USA: MORE AFRICAN STATES ASK FOR PEACEKEEPING TRAINING - U.S..
newsitem.headline: MORE AFRICAN STATES ASK FOR PEACEKEEPING TRAINING - U.S..

text.p: Malawi, Ethiopia and Mali have become the latest African states to accept a U.S. offer for training of peacekeeping units, a senior State Department official said on Tuesday.
About 120 troops from the Army's Ft. Bragg, North Carolina-based 3rd Special Forces Group flew to Senegal and Uganda last week in the first phase of the U.S.-sponsored training programme.
The Americans will train and equip battalion-size units in a programme Washington hopes will boost African states' ability to mount a collective response to humanitarian and other crises.

Marshall McCallie, the State Department's special coordinator for the so-called African Crisis Response Initiative, said training in Malawi was scheduled to start in late September followed by that in Ethiopia and Mali in subsequent months.

"We're getting a lot of interest," he told reporters at the Pentagon at a joint briefing with Col. David McCracken, commander of the 3rd Special Forces Group. "Frankly, the interest will exceed our budget."
For this year, the United States has earmarked $15 million for the programme.

McCallie said the United States hoped to involve other countries in Africa and elsewhere in a multinational training initiative. He said the United States was working closely with France and Britain, but acknowledged it was a "fairly sensitive process" because of fallout from the colonial past.
